title: Audit Patchset Envelope and Identity Confidence Model for RBAC Admin Actions
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Define a compact, mergeable audit "patchset" envelope and an identity confidence model tailored to RBAC admin actions and SSO/SAML assertions. The goal is a consistent event shape that captures what changed (field-level minimal patch), contextual pre/post hints for rapid triage, and a small set of signals for actor confidence to drive downstream alerting and automated policy enforcement.
background: Current audit events vary between full snapshots and ad-hoc diffs. This causes noisy storage, slow queries for change intent, and difficulty attributing admin actions when SAML/SSO and role inheritance are involved. We need a canonical, deltas-first format with provenance fields that answer: who initiated the action, through what identity chain, what minimal state changed, and how confident we are that the actor legitimately authorized the operation.
goals: Define a stable JSON event envelope that is compact and queryable
Standardize a patchset format (add/replace/remove) optimized for admin ops
Include actor provenance and a lightweight identity confidence score with explainable signals
Ensure privacy: redact PII and SAML payloads where required, while preserving traceability
Provide a migration plan (dual-write, backfill index) and criteria for GA rollout
proposed_event_envelope: Fields (top-level): event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, actor_summary, actor_provenance_ids, actor_confidence, auth_context_refs, target_summary, patchset, pre_hints, post_hints, change_reason, request_id, trace_id, retention_class. All fields are optional strings except where noted; arrays represented as list-of-strings. patchset is a compact string encoding (see patch_format).
patch_format: We propose a minimal JSON Patch-like ops array encoded as a compact string to avoid flexible nesting in storage. Each op is encoded as a single line: OP|path|value where OP in [ADD, REPLACE, REMOVE]. Examples: "REPLACE|/roles/3/permissions/2|write:instances", "REMOVE|/members/45|". For large binary/blob diffs (policy blobs), compute a delta and store base64-encoded patch blob as a PASSTHROUGH op: PASSTHROUGH|/policy_blob|<base64-delta>. Patch ordering is canonical: lexicographic by path then op priority (REMOVE, REPLACE, ADD).
actor_provenance_and_identity: actor_summary: human-readable short label (e.g., 'alice@company.com (admin) via SSO'). actor_provenance_ids: list of artifact ids used to link identities (saml_assertion_id, oidc_token_hash, session_id, device_id). auth_context_refs: pointers to SAML assertion record or audit envelope snapshots stored separately (ids). Use these to recreate full assertion if required by compliance. We redact full assertion in the main event and store only reference ids and hashes.
identity_confidence_model: actor_confidence is low/medium/high as a single token plus an explanation list. Confidence signals: SSO_MFA (boolean), SAML_ASSERTION_ISSUER_TRUST (enum), ASSERTION_AGE_SECONDS (numeric hint), DEVICE_POSTURE (enum), IP_RISK_SCORE (numeric hint), ROLE_INHERITANCE_DEPTH (numeric). The event should include a short natural-language explanation entries list describing why the rating was assigned (e.g., 'MFA absent', 'session age > 24h', 'assertion issuer trusted'). We store the short explanation strings in post_hints to help reviewers and automated rules.
pre_post_hints: pre_hints/post_hints are small maps encoded as semi-colon-separated key=value pairs (string). They are NOT exhaustive snapshots but capture fields most helpful for triage: roles_count=3;admin_flag=true;allow_listed_ip=false;policy_version=2025-11-01. Use hints to power quick-change UIs without fetching full snapshots.
redaction_policy: PII (email, phone) in actor_summary is allowed only as hashed form or truncated display. SAML assertions and OIDC tokens MUST NOT be embedded in the main event. Store a single-way hash (SHA256) of the assertion and a pointer to the secure artifact store (auth_context_refs). For export or legal holds, allow retrieval under strict RBAC and audit of access.
indexing_and_query_strategy: Index fields: event_id, tenant_id, timestamp, actor_id_hash, target_id, op_types (inverted), actor_confidence, request_id. For queries that need field-level prior values, provide a side-index mapping event_id->pre_hints. Avoid indexing full patch text. Provide a small parser service to expand compact patch lines to JSON Patch for UI and incident responders.
migration_plan: 1) Dual-write: patchset envelope and current snapshot for 4 weeks. 2) Backfill: run a bounded backfill to convert recent 90 days of snapshot-based audits into patchset envelope using heuristics; mark backfilled events. 3) Reader migration: update console and incident tools to read patchset envelope first, fallback to snapshot. 4) Retention rollout: sample conversion for older events and then apply full retention policy. Rollout tracked under project RBAC-v2 with a feature flag 'audit.patchset.v1'.
storage_and_retention: Retention classes: ephemeral (30d), standard (365d), compliance (7y). The main envelope follows tenant-level retention; auth_context_refs point to secure artifact store with separate retention. For high-volume tenants, allow patch sampling: aggregate low-risk events into summary records instead of storing granular patches. Compliance retention overrides sampling.
examples_and_edge_cases: Edge: role inheritance change where effective permissions are unchanged -> record minimal REMOVE/ADD on inheritance edge and include computed_effect delta hint
Edge: bulk membership imports -> use aggregate summary op AGGREGATE_IMPORT|/members|count=1200 and store a link to the import artifact
Edge: policy binary blobs -> use PASSTHROUGH op with base64 delta and store checksum; require a size threshold (e.g., >4KB) to trigger passthrough
Edge: delegated admin via external SAML attribute -> include delegation_chain in actor_provenance_ids and mark actor_confidence low if delegation unverified
access_and_exports: Exports (for security/forensics) must preserve redaction policy. When exporting events for legal/incident teams, require explicit authorization and log the export in a separate audit channel. Provide an 'expand' API that reconstructs human-readable patches by dereferencing auth_context_refs and the artifact store; this API itself is audited.
acceptance_criteria: Schema document + canonical example reviewed and approved by SecEng, Platform, and Console teams
Reader service can expand compact patchset to JSON Patch and render in Console for a selected event
Writer library implements envelope and enforces redaction rules; dual-write toggled in prod behind a feature flag
Backfill prototype converts 90 days of snapshot events with accuracy > 95% for admin-change intent classification
Indexing pipeline exposes actor_confidence and op_types for alerting rules
implementation_notes: Start with a small internal-only flag for audit.patchset.v1. Implement writer shim in audit-sdk to emit both old and new envelopes. Add validation unit tests that fail on non-canonical ordering or forbidden PII. Provide console formatter that highlights confidence signals and links to auth_context artifacts.
open_questions: What is the canonical list of ops beyond ADD/REPLACE/REMOVE/AGGREGATE/PASSTHROUGH?
Do we want numeric actor_confidence or enumerated low/medium/high? (enumerated preferred for simplicity)
How do we index delegation_chain efficiently without exploding cardinality?
What explicit retention for auth_context_refs fits legal/compliance needs across regions?
links: incidents: INC-3212 (related escalation used as example)
notes: This format emphasizes delta-first storage, explicit provenance, and a minimal confidence model to reduce noise and accelerate incident response. The final shape must be reviewed by Legal for export and by Compliance for retention requirements.
